result.note: Official trade data release; tested the direction of the deficit, its five-month-high status and the import drivers.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's merchandise trade data for June 2026, released in July 2026:
items: Merchandise exports fell year-on-year, which widened the trade deficit.
The merchandise trade deficit of USD 30.43 billion was a five-month high.
Imports of petroleum, gold and electronics drove the widening of the deficit.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because exports rose 15.5% in June 2026; the deficit widened because imports grew faster. The deficit reached USD 30.43 billion, a five-month high and 59% higher year-on-year.
questions.source: up 59% year-on-year as petroleum, gold, and electronics imports outran a 15.5% rise in exports.
